findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on IO failure (missing file, permissions, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and use fs::read_to_string(path) without unwrap, propagating the error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric field values
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV data (e.g., text in the value column) aborts the program instead of returning a parse error
findings.fix: use parse::<u32>().map_err(...) and propagate as a typed domain error

findings.problem: as u16 cast after parse truncates any u32 value > 65535 silently
findings.failure_mode: data corruption: values like 70000 silently wrap to 4464, producing incorrect records with no error
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(...) to reject out-of-range values with a typed error

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] are accessed via unchecked indexing with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV lines (e.g., empty lines or lines with fewer than 2 commas) panic with index out of bounds
findings.fix: use parts.get(0) and parts.get(1) and return a typed error for malformed lines, or restructure with split_once

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a full Vec of all fields when only first two are needed
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation and iteration; also makes the code vulnerable to malformed lines with unexpected field counts
findings.fix: use split_once(',') for first-delimiter extraction, then trim each part individually

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side-effecting I/O call inside what should be pure core data parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: hidden I/O in core logic breaks purity, makes the function non-deterministic (stdout ordering), and couples parsing to console output
findings.fix: remove println! from the parsing pipeline; if logging is needed, return metadata alongside Record or push logging to the imperative shell boundary

findings.problem: parts[0].clone() clones a String from the Vec<String> when split_once + trim yields &str directly
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary allocation; can be eliminated by restructuring parsing to borrow &str until final ownership transfer
findings.fix: after split_once, use .trim() on each &str part and pass to Record::new() which can accept owned strings or use Cow

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> instead of Result<Vec<Record>, E>, hiding all failure modes
findings.failure_mode: all failure modes (IO errors, parse errors, malformed lines, overflow) are silently converted to panics; callers have no way to handle errors gracefully
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, SessionError> where SessionError is an enum covering Io, Parse, Malformed, and Overflow variants

findings.problem: no benchmark exists to validate performance characteristics of load_sessions
findings.failure_mode: no empirical evidence that allocation strategy (per-line Vec<String> collection) is acceptable for expected input sizes
findings.fix: add criterion or similar benchmark measuring allocation count, throughput, and memory for typical and boundary input sizes

findings.problem: no try_reserve or capacity planning on intermediate Vec; each line allocates a new Vec<String>
findings.failure_mode: for large inputs this produces O(n) intermediate allocations per line with no reserve strategy
findings.fix: restructure to avoid per-line Vec allocation entirely via split_once, or use try_reserve on outer collector Vec

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions throughput or allocation profile
no profiler data (e.g., cargo-flamegraph or perf) for the parsing hot path
no allocation tracking (e.g., dhat-rs or #[global_allocator] test) for per-line Vec<String> overhead
no second-ring validation: no integration or behavior test exercising malformed CSV inputs
no command-layer evidence: no cargo test, cargo clippy, or cargo fmt output to confirm baseline hygiene
residual_risk: static review only; no commands run. The crate has 7 BLOCKER violations (unwrap, unchecked indexing, lossy cast, I/O in core, no error types) and 1 MISSING evidence gap. The code as written will panic on any missing file, malformed line, non-numeric value, or out-of-range number. A full rewrite returning Result with typed errors, split_once parsing, try_from casts, and removed side effects is required before this code is production-safe.
